title: Git-history upload resume protocol wedges mid-state uploads permanently
wanted_capability: A resumable or abortable git-history upload protocol. begin_history_upload resumes an existing non-terminal upload record with the same descriptor (returns its upload_id), but the collector client always replays the flow from manifest-page upload, which is invalid for a record stuck in missing_records: the result is a permanent 422 invalid_upload_state loop (wampum program repo, every pass from 2026-08-19 to 2026-08-23, ~660 failures/day). Either the begin response should carry the resumed record's state so the client can continue from the right step, or the client needs an abort/restart verb. Separately, terminal ready/superseded upload staging dirs are never cleaned: 47 leftover ready records had accumulated for one producer (34 for one actively-developed repo). Remedy tonight: deleted the stuck staging dir by hand in the pod; the next collector pass re-uploaded fresh.
missing_primitive: upload state in begin response, or an abort-upload verb, plus terminal-upload staging GC
fallback_used: Manual rm -rf of the stuck upload staging dir in the daemon pod.
evidence: collector log: ~660/day 422 invalid_upload_state on wampum program since 2026-08-19
